facts.text: CrFeNiMo, Co0.5CrFeNiMo, and Al0.5CrFeNiMo powders were SPS-consolidated at 950/1000/1050 °C, 900/950/1000 °C, and 850/900/950 °C, respectively.
CrFeNiMo sintered at 1050 °C, Co0.5CrFeNiMo at 1000 °C, and Al0.5CrFeNiMo at 950 °C were selected as electrodes for depositing either three-layer or six-layer coatings on C1018 steel.
SPS was performed at 50 MPa with 50 °C/min heating, a 5 min dwell, and 30 °C/min cooling in graphite tooling.
Electrospark deposition was conducted under Ar flowing at 5 L/min with the electrode held at approximately 45°.
Increasing SPS temperature promoted particle diffusion, elemental homogenization, densification, and pore closure.
The SPS-consolidated alloys retained composition-dependent multiphase structures with severe lattice distortion, including tetragonally distorted cubic phases.
During ESD, pulsed spark melting transferred electrode material and locally mixed it with the steel surface to form a continuous adherent HEA layer.
Repeated rapid heating and cooling during multilayer ESD generated residual stress, while phase/lattice changes and reduced ductility contributed to roughness and superficial microfissures.

Relative to the lowest SPS temperature for each composition, higher SPS temperatures generally reduced porosity and improved structural integrity and elemental distribution; CrFeNiMo hardness nevertheless decreased slightly at 1050 °C relative to 1000 °C.

The selected CrFeNiMo, Co0.5CrFeNiMo, and Al0.5CrFeNiMo electrodes had densification/porosity/hardness values of 96.876%/3.124%/891.42±8.89 HV, 96.736%/3.264%/790.74±6.22 HV, and 89.014%/10.986%/530±28.73 HV, respectively.

Compared with three-layer coatings, six-layer coatings gave more complete coverage but were generally rougher, more oxidized, and more affected by pores or superficial microfissures; deposited mass ceased increasing after the sixth layer.

dropped.text: The ESD electrical settings were 30 µF/100 V/360 Hz for CrFeNiMo and 20 µF/100 V at 850 Hz or 360 Hz for the Co- and Al-containing alloys, respectively.
